page: Microsoft Azure E96-48ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configuration featuring a constrained vCPU allocation on a large-footprint host. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provides 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores with multithreading. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, delivering a dense 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, supported by 260 MB of L3 cache as well as hardware acceleration instructions including Intel AMX and AVX-512.

Local I/O performance is backed by an integrated 5,669 GB NVMe SSD scratch disk. Across standardized benchmarks, the instance demonstrates strong throughput, achieving 67.4 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and a score of 24,034.71 in PassMark database operations. Geekbench results include a single-core score of 2,149.0 and a multi-core score of 18,862.0, while memory subsystem evaluation shows uncached large-block read bandwidth of 234.94 GB/sec.

Because the server packages 768 GB of memory into 48 vCPUs rather than the full 96-core socket complement, it offers licensing efficiency for software billed on a per-core basis. The platform contains no dedicated GPU hardware, but its matrix and vector extensions sustain prompt processing for inference. This hardware profile is well suited for large in-memory key-value databases, transactional relational database management systems, data processing pipelines, and memory-intensive analytics workloads requiring expansive NVMe temporary capacity.
description: Microsoft Azure E96-48ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores and 768.0 GB of RAM, providing an elevated 16.0 GB of memory per core. Operating on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz, it features 260 MB of L3 cache along with AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. A bundled 5,669 GB NVMe SSD delivers high-capacity local temporary storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight strong data handling capabilities, including 67.4 million Redis SET operations per second, a PassMark database score of 24,034.71, and 234.94 GB/sec uncached large-block read memory bandwidth. Lacking discrete GPUs, this instance optimizes per-core software licensing costs for memory-heavy operations, making it suitable for in-memory databases, large-scale caching tiers, transactional workloads, and data analytics tasks requiring substantial RAM and rapid local scratch disks.
